summary: Preinstall hook downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The npm preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub releases URL, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727KB single-line file `math_init.js` sitting at the tarball root. `math_init.js` shows obfuscator.io fingerprints (rotating string array, ~1000-entry lookup table, hex-mangled identifiers) and is not declared in `package.json` `files` (only `lib/*` is), yet ships in the tarball. The preinstall entrypoint `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated with `_0x`-mangled identifiers and property-lookup dispatch tables wrapping `execFileSync` and `https.get`. The package's advertised purpose is a Vue timestring-input validator; executing an unrelated obfuscated payload under a freshly-fetched alien runtime at install time bypasses Node-based scanners and is functionally unrelated to input validation. The alternate-runtime-dropper delivers unreviewable code execution on the installer's machine on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
